model_reported.name: evaluer-performances
model_reported.summary: Compared the two valid nearby timings cautiously and left correctness and full-call performance evaluation to the controller.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use the valid four-stream variants as nearby references, but do not infer a robust gain from their small timing difference; this experiment tests a larger work-per-thread change.
memory_lessons.claim: The recorded four-accumulator candidate and its separated-tail variant were both valid and measured 0.295090 ms and 0.294029 ms respectively. The modest difference motivates testing a contrasting accumulator count rather than assuming tail handling alone is a meaningful improvement.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this eight-stream mapping with the full correctness suite and full-call timing; if register pressure regresses time, compare a lower stream count.

proposal.hypothesis: Compared with the valid four-accumulator parent, eight independent per-thread streams halve the full-group loop trips and may improve instruction-level parallelism while preserving the 1024-CTA, 256-thread lane ownership, input coverage, partial count, and finalizer. Extra live accumulators may instead increase register pressure; controller correctness and full-call measurements will decide.

retained: Keep 1024 CTAs, 256 threads per CTA, per-lane starting indices, global stride, 1024 partials, and the existing CUB finalizer unchanged.
Replace four independent per-thread accumulators with eight, processing complete groups without per-element bounds checks and checking the remaining tail loads individually.
Retain the two-kernel fused absolute-sum topology and write each partial and output on every call.
